title: Al-Fatiha, again
hookLine: the mother of the book, now heard with thirty surahs behind it

lines: SEVEN LINES, MET AS A BEGINNER.
HEARD AGAIN, WITH A JUZ' BEHIND THEM.
cards: Some songs you heard as a kid mean something completely different when you hear them at forty. The words haven't changed. You have.
In the first weeks of this path, you met the Fatiha, the opening, seven short lines said in every unit of every prayer. You learned them as a beginner does, one phrase at a time.
Since then you've read the whole last part of the Qur'an: the Day of sorting, the orphan, the whisperer, the Living who does not sleep.
So today the path goes back to the start, to hear the same seven lines with thirty-seven surahs standing behind them.

teach.b: Bukhari records the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ calling the Fatiha umm al-Qur'an, the mother of the Qur'an, and the seven oft-repeated verses. Umm al-kitab: the mother of the book.
In Arabic, umm is a mother, and also a source, the thing that gathers everything around it; a region's capital can be called its umm. Now listen with the juz' behind you.

teach.h: LORD, MERCIFUL, OWNER OF THE DAY.
teach.b: Pickthall: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, The Beneficent, the Merciful. Owner of the Day of Judgment. Lord of the worlds: An-Naba' pointed at the earth as a bed and the mountains as pegs.
The Beneficent, the Merciful: nearly every surah opened with those two names. Owner of the Day of Judgment: the Day of sorting, the trumpet, what the hands sent ahead.
Then: Thee alone we worship, Thee alone we ask for help. Show us the straight path. The juz' spent pages on that path: purify the soul, feed the orphan, don't push anyone away.
The Fatiha is the whole book folded small, and the book is the Fatiha unfolded.
And remember the hadith qudsi from the first week, and again from the standing in the prayer: in Muslim's collection, Allah divides the prayer between Himself and His servant.
My servant has praised Me. You heard it as a beginner. Now the praise that is answered is praise of the Lord who spread the earth like a bed and kept the orphan in view.
In the tradition's telling, at each line, an answer.

how: Muslims recite al-Fatiha in every unit of every prayer, at least seventeen times a day in the obligatory prayers, and also at weddings, over the sick, and in remembrance of the dead; many learn its meaning line by line to recite it with attention.

o: the longest surah, al-Baqarah, in full
a name for the Fatiha: mother of the book
the first written copy of the Qur'an

games.q: the Fatiha and the juz' — tap the pairs.
p: the earth a bed, mountains as pegs
purify the soul, feed the orphan

s: the phrase umm al-kitab is used only for the Fatiha
the Qur'an also uses it for the clear verses (3:7) and the source of the book with Allah (43:4).
in a hadith qudsi, Allah answers each line of the Fatiha
Muslim: My servant has praised Me, and so on through the lines.
the Fatiha is recited only in the first unit of the prayer

games.q: the servant says, praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. in the hadith qudsi, what happens?
o: Allah says, My servant has praised Me
an angel writes it down silently
games.why: Allah divides the prayer between Himself and His servant and answers each line (Sahih Muslim).

practice: Take the Fatiha slowly, one line per breath, in Arabic or in English, and beside each line let one picture from the juz' come up: Lord of the worlds, the mountains as pegs; the Merciful, the orphan found and sheltered; Owner of the Day, the earth telling its news; the straight path, a hungry orphan fed.
If you pray, you can let today's prayers go a little slower at the Fatiha.

wordCard.voice: Umm al-kitab. The mother of the book, a name for the Fatiha: the source that gathers the whole Qur'an into seven lines. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the mother of the book, a name for al-Fatiha.

carryVoice: Your line: the mother of the book. Seven lines, heard with new ears. Day two hundred twenty-six, done.

sources.q: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, The Beneficent, the Merciful. Owner of the Day of Judgment,
